literature_notes: The ledger contains two clips (L1, L2) both describing the same construct: Lrrc8b smFPMyclox, a knock-in mouse in which a spaghetti-monster FP and Myc epitope tag are fused to full-length, membrane-anchored LRRC8B. This satisfies the 'full-length membrane-anchored' requirement. However, neither clip names a residue, a loop, or a terminus at which the tag is inserted. The topology_derived rule (which would allow position inference without a named residue) applies only when exactly ONE terminus is extracellular — but LRRC8B has both its N-terminus (residues 1–23) and C-terminus (residues 337–803) on the intracellular face. No extracellular terminus exists from which to derive a junction. The region-level rule requires a named loop, which neither clip provides. Because no positional anchor — residue, loop name, or sole extracellular terminus — is present in the ledger, no extracellular surface site can be proposed. The smFP/Myc tag most likely resides at an intracellular terminus (consistent with LRRC8 family practice), but even that cannot be confirmed from the clips. Zero sites is the correct answer.
